text.name: The desktop grid system provides a consistent structure for aligning and organizing content across the platform. Our desktop layout uses a 12-column grid with a 120px margin and 32px gutter within a 1440px frame. This grid helps maintain consistent spacing, alignment, and visual hierarchy across desktop interfaces.

The large desktop grid system provides a consistent structure for organizing and aligning content across wider screens. Our large desktop layout uses a 12-column grid with a 140px margin and 32px gutter within a 1920px frame. This grid helps maintain consistent spacing, alignment, and visual hierarchy across large-screen interfaces.

The mobile grid system provides a flexible structure for organizing and aligning content across smaller screens. Our mobile layout uses a 4-column grid with a 16px margin and 16px gutter within a 360px frame. This grid helps maintain consistent spacing, alignment, and visual hierarchy across mobile interfaces.
Use the mobile grid for compact app interfaces and standard responsive phone viewports. Align key content and interactive items to column boundaries while maintaining the defined safe margins.
Use the desktop grid for web applications, landing pages, and content-dense tables. Use multiple columns to establish visual hierarchy and alignment.
Apply to large-screen monitors where available space is available. Maintains defined column span content width and preserves visual focus on applications and content.
More screen space provides greater layout flexibility while maintaining consistent alignment, spacing, and content structure.
Use the appropriate grid based on the target frame size.
Align major page sections and components to the grid.
Maintain the defined gutter between columns.
Respect the defined left and right margins.
Use column spans to establish content hierarchy.
Keep component alignment consistent across sections.
Preserve grid relationships when designing responsive layouts.
Use the grid as a structural foundation, not a visual constraint.
